name: read_nested_field_or_zero
description: Returns zero when the pointer passed in the address register is null. Otherwise it follows two pointer fields in the structure and returns the longword stored at the end of that chain.

name: resolve_disk_info_path
description: Builds a path in a stack buffer from a base string and the text disk.info that the library references, then runs a lookup on it. If the lookup fails and a flag byte is set, it falls back to a value read through nested pointers and records in a global flag whether that fallback was used.

name: check_status_and_set_flag
description: Runs a library call on a stack buffer using a field from a structure, then checks its return value and a flag byte. If both indicate success it sets a global flag to one and returns a longword read through a nested pointer; otherwise it clears the flag and returns the call's result.

name: allocate_and_fill_record
description: Allocates a cleared block through a library call and a second block after it, then checks them against a shared state structure. On success it sizes a new record to at least 256, fills it from copied fields and returns one; any failure returns zero.

name: populate_record_from_allocation
description: Stores a freshly obtained handle, then if the shared state and the optional argument pass their checks it copies a block into the record, sizes it to at least 256 and allocates a buffer. It fills the buffer's fields and returns one when the allocation succeeded, otherwise zero.

name: populate_record_fields
description: Checks a shared-state flag and an optional argument, then copies a block into the record, sizes it to at least 256 and allocates a buffer. On success it fills the buffer's fields and returns one, otherwise zero.

name: populate_record_if_valid
description: Runs only when the optional argument is clear or a library check passes, then copies a block into the record, sizes it to at least 256, allocates a buffer and fills its fields. Returns one on success and zero when the allocation fails.

name: fill_record_and_report_success
description: Copies a block into the record, sizes it to at least 256 and allocates a buffer. It fills the buffer's fields and returns whether the allocation succeeded.

name: copy_library_strings_and_data
description: Copies a string from the shared state into the record through a library routine, then copies two longword fields from the state and the entry into the record. Always returns one.

name: setup_library_state_error_codes
description: Clears a set of shared globals and stores the argument, then requests a resource tagged 246 and runs further checks and library calls to set up the working buffers. Failures are reported as error codes through a routine; success links the buffers together and returns.

name: setup_library_buffers_via_callback
description: Requests a resource tagged 246, then obtains a second buffer and a shared global. It links them with library calls and reports success or an error code through a callback register.

name: finish_library_buffer_setup
description: Checks a stack record, then obtains a shared global and links it to a buffer using library calls. It reports the outcome through a callback register, with success when the final checks pass.

name: link_library_buffer_or_fail
description: Obtains a handle and, if it is valid, allocates a shared buffer and links it to the handle through library calls. Any failure reports an error code through a callback register, and success calls the callback with zero.

name: attach_shared_buffer_callback
description: Obtains a shared buffer and copies a field from the record into it. It then runs a library call and, when the result is nonzero, performs four library calls to finish linking, reporting success or an error code through a callback.

name: finish_library_link_and_notify
description: Copies a field from the record into a shared buffer and runs a library call. If the shared flag and the argument allow it and the check passes, it performs four library calls and reports success; otherwise it reports error code one.

name: notify_library_link_result
description: Obtains a handle and checks it. It either reports error one through a callback, or on success performs four library calls and reports zero.

name: complete_library_link_success
description: When a shared flag is clear and an argument is set, it runs a library call on the handle. It then performs four library calls and reports success through a callback.

name: call_library_vector_132
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 132 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_138
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 138 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_198
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 198 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_210
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 210 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_246
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 246 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_294
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 294 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_372
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 372 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_378
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 378 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_414
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 414 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_552
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 552 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_42
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 42 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_96
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 96 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_228
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 228 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: invoke_callback_from_table
description: Takes a routine from a global table of function pointers at a fixed offset and calls it. It performs no other work before returning.

name: call_library_vector_462
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 462 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_72
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 72 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_78
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 78 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_indirect_through_table
description: Reads a routine pointer from a global table at a fixed negative offset and calls it indirectly. It performs no other work before returning.

name: call_indirect_table_entry
description: Calls a routine through a pointer read from a global table at a fixed offset, then returns. It is a pass-through stub with no arguments of its own.

name: call_library_vector_354
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 354 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: build_parameter_block_and_call
description: Fills a stack-allocated block with numeric values and a pointer to a global, then passes it to a library call. If that call returns a non-zero handle, it calls a second library function with that handle and the global pointer, then returns the handle.

name: dispatch_state_code_actions
description: Reads a state code from a nested structure and branches on it, performing the matching library call and updating a stored flag in some cases. It returns zero for the failing states and one for the rest.

name: return_success_stub
description: Returns one unconditionally with no other work. It is a success stub in the library code.

name: toggle_status_bit_from_code
description: Maps a code read from a structure to one bit value, flips that bit in a stored state word and saves it back. Unlisted codes leave the word unchanged, and the argument's follow-up routine is then called.

name: store_register_to_global
description: Stores the value passed in a data register into a fixed field of the shared state, then calls a routine with a pointer read from the argument structure. It returns nothing.

name: format_info_file_and_check
description: Builds a file name in a stack buffer from the referenced pattern with the suffix .info, then runs several library calls on it and on the shared state. It returns true only when the lookups and conditional checks all succeed.

name: validate_disk_entry_name
description: Builds a name in a stack buffer from the referenced text Disk or a stored string, then tests it with a library call. When a state byte is not one, it also checks two more library results before returning a combined success flag.

name: copy_name_and_verify_attributes
description: Copies a string from the shared state into a stack buffer and tests it with a library call. If a state byte is not one, it runs two more library calls and an attribute mask check, returning zero whenever a test fails.

name: verify_four_handles_then_commit
description: Runs four library calls with the same argument, each checked for a failure value of minus one. If any one fails it returns zero; otherwise it runs a follow-up routine and returns one.

name: verify_three_indirect_calls
description: Calls a routine held in a register three times, returning zero if any call returns minus one. When all three succeed it runs one follow-up routine and returns one.

name: verify_two_indirect_calls
description: Calls a routine held in a register twice, returning zero if either call returns minus one. Otherwise it runs one follow-up routine and returns one.

name: run_indirect_call_if_ok
description: Calls a routine held in a register and, if its result is not minus one, runs one follow-up routine. It returns true when the call result was not minus one.

name: call_other_and_return_one
description: Calls one routine and then returns one with no other checks. It is a simple success wrapper.

name: initialize_info_library_tables
description: Registers a long sequence of entries by calling one routine with fixed numeric ranges and a pointer from the argument, and passes a global as the last argument for three entries. The referenced titles NAME, STATUS and TYPE suggest the entries are column headings.

name: register_seven_fixed_ranges
description: Calls one routine seven times with the same first argument and constant range pairs. It returns nothing.

name: register_seven_index_ranges
description: Calls one routine seven times with the same first argument and constant index pairs, several of which share bounds. It returns nothing.

name: register_nine_index_ranges
description: Calls one routine nine times with the same first argument and constant index pairs. It returns nothing.

name: set_nine_index_ranges
description: Calls one routine nine times, passing the same first argument with six constant values each time. It returns nothing.

name: populate_entries_by_state_code
description: Chooses one of two numeric values from a state code, then adds either a fixed entry set or a longer one depending on whether a list is empty. When the second argument is nonzero it adds one more entry using a stored pointer.

name: finish_list_update_conditionally
description: Runs one of two routine calls depending on whether a list is empty, then runs one more call with a global only when the flag argument is nonzero. It returns nothing.

name: run_update_steps_with_option
description: Calls a library function, then calls another routine with a field from a structure, and calls a third time with a global when an option register is set. It returns nothing.

name: allocate_linked_entry_list
description: Allocates a cleared entry and links it to itself as the head of a list. If the shared state holds a table of pointers, it allocates an entry for each one, copies the pointer into it and links it in; it returns the head, or zero when an allocation fails.

name: link_entries_from_table
description: Points the list head to itself and clears a counter, then for each pointer in a shared table it allocates an entry, copies the table value into it and links it in. It returns early if an allocation fails.

name: link_entries_until_null_pointer
description: Walks a null-terminated table, allocating an entry for each pointer and linking it into the list with library calls. It returns zero if an allocation fails, otherwise it sets the list head and returns the last result.

name: link_table_entries_to_end
description: Links each table entry in turn, allocating a fresh entry per pointer and copying the table value into it. When the table ends it sets the list head and returns the last result, or zero if an allocation fails.

name: advance_list_cursor_or_finish
description: If the current list position is at an end point, it runs closing calls using fields of the argument structure. Otherwise it processes the current entry, moves the position to the next entry and runs a final call.

name: update_pointer_from_structure
description: Runs a routine on the current entry and a fixed global, then copies the next link of the entry into the cursor and runs one more call. It returns nothing.

name: advance_cursor_or_restart
description: If the cursor is at an end point, it runs closing calls on the argument structure. Otherwise it processes the current entry, moves the cursor to the entry's first link and runs a final call.

name: update_pointer_dereference
description: Runs a routine on the current entry and a fixed global, then replaces the cursor with the value its first link points to and runs two more calls. It returns nothing.

name: insert_new_entry_at_cursor
description: Sets a flag and, when the list has entries, runs two calls on the current entry. It then allocates a new entry with a sub-block, links it in at the cursor, makes it the cursor and runs a final call with the flag set to one.

name: move_cursor_to_neighbour_entry
description: Sets a flag, then either runs the finishing calls when the list is at its end or processes the current entry. It runs one call on the old cursor entry and moves the cursor to a neighbouring entry.

name: reset_cursor_to_first_entry
description: Records the first link of the cursor entry and runs a call on the cursor. When the list is at its end it takes the first link of the list instead, stores the chosen entry as the new cursor and runs one more call.

name: run_three_step_callbacks
description: Calls one routine with no argument, then calls two more with fields of the argument structure. It returns nothing.

name: build_pointer_array_from_list
description: When a flag is set and the list is not empty, it counts the entries, allocates an array of pointers sized to match and stores it in the shared state. It then fills each slot by allocating a block and linking it to that entry, returning zero if any allocation fails.

name: populate_pointer_array_for_list
description: Allocates a pointer array sized to the list length and stores it in the shared state, or clears the array field when the list is empty. Each slot then receives an allocated block linked to one entry, and the routine returns zero on allocation failure.

name: fill_pointer_array_from_entries
description: Calls a routine on the cursor, counts the list entries and allocates an array sized to the count, storing it in the shared state. It then allocates a block for each entry and links it, returning one on success and zero on any allocation failure.

name: allocate_pointer_array_for_entries
description: Counts entries from a starting count and allocates an array sized to that count, storing it in the shared state. For each list entry it then allocates a block and links it, returning one on success and zero on any allocation failure.

name: link_entries_into_pointer_array
description: Calls a routine with the pointer array from the shared state, then walks the list allocating a block per entry and linking it into the array. It returns one when the walk finishes and zero if an allocation fails.

name: link_remaining_entries_in_array
description: Continues from the current list entry, allocating a block for each remaining entry and linking it into the pointer array. It returns one when the list ends and zero if an allocation fails.

name: continue_linking_array_entries
description: Links the remaining entries into the array, allocating a block for each one and stopping at the end of the list. It returns one when the list is exhausted and zero when an allocation fails.

name: call_library_vector_90
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 90 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: dispatch_entries_by_state_byte
description: Switches on a state byte from the shared state and runs a different set of routine calls for each case. The calls pass numeric pairs and pointers from the shared state, and some cases end with a final call.

name: return_empty_stub
description: Returns immediately with no work. It is an empty stub in the library code.

name: allocate_buffers_setup_by_state
description: Allocates four buffers and, if all succeed, allocates four more. It then switches on a state byte and performs a case-specific set of setup calls, returning the final call's result, the state byte in the default case, or zero when an allocation fails.

name: store_handles_run_by_state
description: Calls a routine held in a register four times, keeping three results in globals and the fourth through a pointer. If any result is zero it returns zero; otherwise it runs a different number of follow-up calls for each state byte and returns that byte.

name: run_calls_by_state_byte
description: Runs a different number of follow-up routine calls for each state byte value from one to five. It takes no arguments and returns nothing.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. It is a no-operation stub in the library code.

name: clear_field_then_query_status
description: Clears a stored value if a field is zero, or passes the field to a library call otherwise. It then runs a library call on the argument and returns zero when the result is minus one, otherwise the result.

name: pass_field_then_return_result
description: Passes a stored field to a library call together with a global, then runs another call and returns zero when its result is minus one, otherwise that result.

name: return_nothing_stub
description: Returns without doing anything. It is an empty stub in the library code.

name: set_offsets_verify_four_calls
description: Writes four fixed 16-bit values into structures at a fixed offset when the state byte is not four, then runs four library calls checked against minus one. It returns one if all succeed and zero otherwise.

name: verify_three_register_calls
description: Calls a routine held in a register three times, returning zero if any call returns minus one. Otherwise it returns one.

name: verify_two_register_calls
description: Calls a routine held in a register twice, returning zero if either call returns minus one. Otherwise it returns one.

name: check_register_call_succeeds
description: Calls a routine held in a register and returns true when the result is not minus one.

name: return_one_stub
description: Returns one with no other work. It is a success stub in the library code.

name: poll_bit_signal_loop
description: Repeatedly calls a library function to fetch a value from a structure. Each non-zero value is passed to a second call, and a failure there returns zero; when no value is found, a single bit chosen by a byte in the structure is passed to a routine.

name: return_failure_stub
description: Returns zero with no other work. It is a failure stub in the library code.

name: dispatch_on_size_code
description: Reads a numeric code from a structure and branches on it. Code four runs one routine on a field, code 64 returns the result of a routine that takes the second argument, and code 512 runs a routine and returns zero; other codes run a default routine and return one.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Calls one routine with no argument and returns nothing.

name: call_routine_return_zero
description: Calls one routine with no argument and returns zero.

name: execute_two_calls
description: Calls two routines in sequence and returns one. It performs no other work.

name: run_callback_sequence_for_state
description: Runs the same routine three times with the argument, adds a fourth call when the state byte is not one, then calls routines with a field from the argument and with a flag value of one. It returns nothing.

name: report_protection_flag_entries
description: Derives four flag bits from a stored status word and calls a routine once per bit with its index and a global pointer. The referenced labels ARCHIVED, DELETEABLE, READABLE and WRITEABLE match the standard file protection flags these entries describe.

name: emit_labelled_flag_entries
description: Builds a short key in a stack buffer from a constant string and a selector, then chooses one of two pairs of text arguments depending on a flag. It then emits two entries built from that buffer, and the referenced pattern with the text NOT points to negated labels.

name: format_string_arguments
description: Packs a stack argument list from the referenced pattern texts and a value taken from the caller's frame, then runs two further routines. It returns nothing.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the bytes of a zero-terminated string from its start and returns the count without the terminator.

name: calculate_string_length
description: Advances an index from a starting register value until a zero byte is found and returns that index as the length.

name: copy_cstring_to_buffer
description: Copies a zero-terminated byte string from a source pointer to a destination pointer, advancing both and writing each byte including the terminator. It returns nothing.

name: copy_fixed_length_bytes
description: Copies a requested number of bytes from a source buffer to a destination, advancing both pointers on each byte. It returns nothing.

name: copy_memory_block
description: Copies a fixed number of bytes from a source pointer to a destination pointer, one byte at a time. It returns nothing.

name: skip_matching_prefix
description: Advances through two strings while their characters match and neither has ended, then returns whether the characters at the stopping point are equal.

name: compare_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings from the input registers, advancing both until a mismatch or an end is reached. It returns true when the final characters are equal.

name: count_bytes_including_terminator
description: Counts the bytes of a zero-terminated string and returns the count including the terminating zero byte.

name: execute_library_operations
description: Calls a routine to obtain a value, then passes a field of the structure to three library calls with arguments adjusted by minus ten and the value obtained earlier. It returns nothing.

name: call_string_formatter
description: Builds a formatted string in a 12-byte local buffer from a global pattern and one argument, then passes that buffer with the other arguments to a second routine. It returns nothing.

name: copy_length_prefixed_string
description: Reads a count from the first byte of the source and copies that many following bytes to the destination, then appends a zero terminator. The addressing is unusual, so this may be data that was decoded as code.

name: copy_string_data
description: Copies bytes from a source location to a destination location for a count held in registers, then writes a zero terminator at the end. It takes its pointers and counts from registers rather than from arguments.

name: initialize_two_records_and_call
description: Fills two record structures with fixed field values, including the argument and a pointer from the caller, then runs two library calls and a third call that returns a status. It runs a follow-up call on success and returns true when the status is not minus one.

name: execute_library_function
description: Passes a pointer stored in a structure at a fixed offset to a library call, then returns one.

name: execute_library_calls
description: Calls one routine with a field of the structure, then calls it again with zero, and a third time with the remaining arguments adjusted by minus ten. It returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_522
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 522 of that base. The analysis identifies that function as the exec formatting routine RawDoFmt.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register into the memory location the address register points to. It returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_36
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 36 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_72
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 72 of that base. It is a pass-through stub that returns nothing.

name: return_zero_entry
description: Returns zero immediately with no other work. It is the entry stub of the version library.

name: store_two_values_at_offsets
description: Writes two 32-bit values held in registers into a structure, one at offset 34 and the other at offset 38. It returns nothing.

name: increment_counter_and_clear_flag
description: Increments a 16-bit counter stored 32 bytes into a structure and clears the eighth bit of a flag byte 42 bytes in. It returns nothing.

name: decrement_counter_and_call
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter stored 32 bytes into a structure. When the counter reaches zero and the flag bit with value eight is set, it calls one routine and returns that result, otherwise it returns zero.

name: finish_when_counter_zero
description: If the counter at offset 32 is zero, it reads the value at offset 38 and calls two library functions through the base stored at offset 34, then returns that value. Otherwise it sets the flag bit with value eight and returns zero.

name: get_library_value
description: Reads a longword at offset 38 of the structure, calls two library functions at fixed negative offsets on the base in a register, and returns the value read.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero with no other work. It is a stub in the version library.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the stack argument pointer is not null, copies 16 longwords from a fixed block in the structure into it. It then calls a routine through a register pointer and returns.

name: setup_command_shell_buffer
description: Walks a list of entries to find the largest stored value, allocates a buffer sized from it and fills it with an increasing series of values. It copies 16 longwords into the buffer and returns zero on success or minus one on failure; this is the same code as the setup routine in the endcli program.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: Copies 16 longwords from a fixed block in the structure into the buffer passed on the stack, then calls a routine through a register pointer and returns. It is the same copy routine as the one in the earlier program file.

name: start_workbench_loader
description: Main program entry of the Workbench loader. It opens the DOS library and related ports, allocates a task structure, parses the command string into arguments, runs the startup routine and then tidies up, returning a result code or 100 when an allocation fails.

name: release_task_resources_and_return
description: Stores the argument in a slot of a shared structure, then conditionally calls cleanup routines that close a file and a library, free memory and reply to a message, with the task locked while it works. It returns the stored argument.

name: start_resident_workbench_tool
description: XORs a global byte string with a fixed key in two passes, which cancels out, then allocates a buffer and fills it with the decoded text. It looks up a resident tag and starts the tool, and the referenced messages Cannot find resident tag and Cannot start tool report the failures.

name: compare_strings_ordered
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one when the first is less than the second, one when it is greater, and zero when they are equal.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of entries, allocating an 8-byte node for each and copying a table value into it, then linking the nodes in order. It returns the head of the new list, or zero when a node cannot be allocated.

name: compare_release_text_and_pad
description: Compares a version string with a global string matching the referenced text Workbench release 1.2, and when the version digit is two and the strings match it writes a dot and four spaces into the buffer. Otherwise it returns without writing.

name: write_dot_and_spaces
description: Writes a period followed by four space characters at fixed positions in a buffer. It returns nothing.

name: compare_prefix_with_global
description: Compares a string in a register with a global string until they differ or the global string ends. It returns nothing; the outcome is left in the registers.

name: return_empty_routine
description: Returns immediately with no operation. It is an empty routine in the program code.

name: call_with_stack_slot_pointer
description: Calls another routine with the two arguments it received plus a pointer to a fixed stack slot. It returns nothing.

name: format_buffer_and_pass_length
description: Calls a library formatting function through a global base, then measures the length of a 140-byte stack buffer up to its terminator. If the length is non-zero it passes the buffer and the length to a routine.

name: setup_command_shell_buffer
description: Walks a list of entries to find the largest stored value, allocates a buffer sized from it and fills it with an increasing series of values. It copies 16 longwords into the buffer and returns zero on success or minus one on failure; this is the same code as the setup routine in the endcli program.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the stack argument pointer is not null, copies 16 longwords from a fixed block in the structure into it. It then calls a routine through a register pointer and returns.

name: run_disk_validator_program
description: Program entry of the disk validator, shown here only in part because the listing is truncated. The visible code fills a table of slots with a series of values, then loops over bit positions, calling library routines and writing results into a block of the structure.

name: clear_state_and_start_game
description: Clears a block of about 28 KB of the program state, stores a library base and a global pointer, and calls a library function when a flag bit is set. It starts the main routine on success and otherwise calls an exit function.

name: initialize_demo_resources
description: Stores handles obtained from library calls into globals, allocates a block of 300 items of size 2 and fills several fields of a structure from register values. It repeats part of the setup when a field of the argument is below two, and the referenced text demo.pic suggests a picture file is loaded.

name: start_copper_list_from_field
description: Passes a pointer read from a structure at a fixed offset to a routine that points the copper at a new copper list by writing the list address to the COP1LC register and strobing COPJMP1 so the list starts at once. It returns nothing.

name: manage_interrupt_enable_flags
description: Calls a series of routines with constant values, including a value for the interrupt enable register INTENA where a set top bit enables interrupts and a cleared top bit disables them. It finally stores a constant in a global variable.

name: create_program_process
description: Creates a 40-byte structure, fills its fields from a global value and a fixed name, then calls library routines that create a process and load a program segment. The referenced text populous.prg and startup names the program it starts.

name: setup_memory_table
description: Allocates a block of 1152 bytes and stores its address in a global. It fills eight table slots with offsets increasing by 144, calls a routine, then copies two values between globals and adds 72 to one of them.

name: store_constant_and_call
description: Stores the constant 399 as a word in a global variable through a register-based pointer, then calls one routine. It returns nothing.

name: call_routine_from_table
description: Passes the block allocated earlier, of size 1152 bytes, to a routine. It returns nothing.

name: call_two_global_pointers
description: Calls one routine with each of two global pointer values, one after the other. It returns nothing.

name: call_library_vector_300
description: Extracts a field from its argument and calls the library function at offset minus 300 of a library base read from a global, passing that field value. It returns nothing.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one routine with no argument and returns nothing.

name: find_matching_entry_and_call
description: Searches a two-entry table in the globals for the argument. When an entry matches it calls one routine with the paired value, and it stores the index reached in a global variable.

name: swap_globals_and_call
description: Swaps two 32-bit values stored in globals, then calls one routine with the swapped values. It returns nothing.

name: initialize_graphics_resources
description: Obtains a base from one routine and stores it in a field, then requests two resources with fixed numbers and makes a further call when either is zero. It records a masked flag from one of them, and the referenced text graphics.library and intuition.library suggests which libraries are involved.

name: wait_for_code_then_dispatch
description: Repeatedly calls a routine until it returns one, two or three, then passes a global and a pointer to a fixed offset to a further routine. It returns nothing.

name: wait_and_classify_load_stage
description: Starts a load routine that references the text load.pic, then waits for up to 350000 loops for a flag to clear. It classifies two position values into one of three ranges and returns that category, or zero when no range matches.

name: initialize_game_state
description: Stores two function pointers in globals, writes three constants, and clears a short array until a zero entry is found. It then sets up a table of 16 records from a global array and loops, toggling a flag and calling routines with table values until a stop value is returned.

name: update_game_tick_entries
description: Runs one tick of updates: it toggles a flag, decrements two timers that reload at 50, and processes 16 entries from a byte table by calling routines for each. The listing is truncated in the job file, so the later branches are not described.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything. It is a no-operation stub in the program code.

name: run_offset_update_loop
description: Fills 18 slots of a table with values masked to three bits, then loops calling routines with positions offset from 160 or 168 minus stored values until an abort byte is set or a counter reaches zero. It returns zero when a check inside the setup fails and one otherwise.

name: fill_short_arrays_modulo
description: Loops over the count given in its argument, filling one 16-bit array with values from 232 to 244 chosen by a routine's result modulo 13, and a second array with values from 0 to 8 chosen modulo 9.

name: update_short_arrays
description: Loops over the count given in its argument, increasing each entry of one array by one and subtracting it from the matching entry of another. Negative results are clamped to zero and the second value is halved, and it returns the first value stored in the second array.

name: process_demo_pic_sequence
description: Makes a sequence of library and routine calls, one of them with a fixed value, then repeats a loop that calls routines while a routine returns nonzero and the abort flags are clear. It finishes by copying pointers and clearing a flag, and the referenced text demo.pic names the picture it works with.

name: initialize_dma_list_entries
description: Fills four list entries with offsets from a base pointer, stepping by 300 for one table and by 32000 for the other, and calls a routine for each entry. It then copies four values from the table into globals.

name: read_block_then_release
description: Obtains a handle through a routine with code 1005, reads 32000 bytes into a global buffer through the read wrapper, copies a second region with another routine and releases the handle. It returns zero on success or minus one when the handle cannot be obtained.

name: load_game_data_files
description: Opens three data files named in the referenced text font.dat, land0 and sprites0.dat, reading several blocks of fixed byte counts from each one and closing each handle. The blocks include a 114-byte header before the first large read.

name: load_optional_file_blocks
description: Opens a file through a routine with code 1005. If that succeeds it reads 40000 bytes into the buffer argument and 64 bytes into a global buffer, then closes the file.

name: rotate_and_combine_word_table
description: Rotates a set of 16-bit words by an amount taken from a nibble of the parameter and combines the results into four interleaved planes of a destination buffer using AND and OR. It repeats this for 32 rows and runs only when the row argument is in range.

name: apply_rotated_mask_to_tiles
description: Uses a value derived from its input to pick a 32-bit mask from a fixed table, rotates it by a nibble amount, then ANDs and ORs the rotated words into four planes of the destination for 16 rows. It runs only when the position argument is in range.

name: call_routine_and_return_pair
description: Calls one routine and returns the two data registers unchanged as a combined 64-bit value.

name: apply_tile_mask_table
description: Applies a mask table entry, indexed by a global and a register value, to four planes of destination words. When the nibble is zero it combines the words directly, otherwise it rotates them first, and it runs 24 rows only when the position is in range.

name: reorder_struct_fields
description: Walks 1680 entries of 20 bytes in a global table and rotates fields between them, moving pairs of 16-bit words and bytes within each entry. The transformed values are written back to the same table.

name: shift_byte_buffer
description: Shifts each of the 100 bytes of a fixed buffer left by three bits. The loop runs a fixed count.

name: place_grid_cells_with_offsets
description: Loops over a 10 by 10 grid, calling a routine with coordinates computed from the row and column and an offset table entry. When a flag byte is set it also calls another routine for each cell.

name: concatenate_registers
description: Calls one routine, then returns the two data registers combined into one 64-bit value. Nothing else happens.

name: set_global_pointer_to_buffer
description: Stores the address of a global buffer in a global pointer variable. The referenced text POPULOUS is not used by this code itself.

name: initialize_buffer_from_string
description: Fills 80 longwords with minus one and then 320 longwords with zero. It then measures a global string and copies five-byte column slices of character data from a fixed table into the buffer, one column per character, advancing a global pointer past the text.

name: open_library_and_set_defaults
description: Opens a library through a global function pointer and, if that fails, runs two cleanup calls through the library base and returns. On success it runs two more library calls, saves three globals, sets globals to the constants 16383 and 49152, clears a byte in a structure and returns.

name: open_library_and_set_defaults
description: Same body as the routine above; the listing repeats the open-and-set-defaults code, so this copy carries no separate logic.

name: stub_single_instruction_entry
description: Single-instruction entry whose decompiled body repeats the open-and-set-defaults code. The repeat is a listing artefact, so this is a stub that passes control on.

name: stub_entry_into_shared_body
description: Single-instruction entry whose decompiled body repeats the open-and-set-defaults code. The repeat is a listing artefact, so this is a stub that passes control on.

name: stub_jump_to_shared_body
description: Single-instruction entry whose decompiled body repeats the open-and-set-defaults code. The repeat is a listing artefact, so this is a stub that passes control on.

name: load_popsam_file
description: The pseudo-code in the job is a copy of the open-and-set-defaults body, so this name rests on the facts list. The routine opens dos.library and a file named popsam, allocates memory and moves data with it, reporting the messages NOT ENOUGH MEMORY and I CANT FIND THE FILE on failure.

name: clear_byte_and_return
description: Stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the address register, then returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: restore_interrupt_state_and_free
description: Sets two globals to 16383, calls a routine and a library function at minus 210 through the base, then writes saved globals back, with the first one OR-ed with 49152. The facts record an exec free-memory call and writes to the interrupt enable and request registers INTENA and INTREQ.

name: dispatch_code_then_clear_byte
description: Calls a routine when the code byte is ten or one, then clears the byte at a fixed offset of the structure and returns the stack value unchanged.

name: clear_byte_after_code_one
description: Calls a routine when the code byte is one, then clears the byte at a fixed offset of the structure and returns the stack value unchanged.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears the byte at a fixed offset of the structure and returns the stack value unchanged. It calls nothing in the shown code.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears the byte at a fixed offset of the structure and returns the stack value unchanged. This is the same code as the neighbouring copy.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears the byte at a fixed offset of the structure and returns the stack value unchanged. This is the same code as the neighbouring copy.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears the byte at a fixed offset of the structure and returns the stack value unchanged. This is the same code as the neighbouring copy.

name: service_interrupt_flag_bit
description: Tests bit five, the value 32, of a global flag and, when it is set, writes 255 to a hardware-related address, stores a masked value back in the flag and calls one routine. The facts record the CIA and interrupt registers INTENAR, INTREQ and INTREQR as touched.

name: build_period_and_dispatch_tables
description: Builds tables from a global block: for each of seven records it stores a pointer and a period value computed by dividing 3579545 by a word, then fills pointer entries and four dispatch entries. It finishes by writing 255 to a byte.

name: build_dispatch_tables
description: Builds dispatch tables from a global block using the same logic as the routine just before it: a period value is computed by dividing 3579545 by a word for each record, and pointer entries are filled from a table. The listing repeats that body.

name: reset_global_flags
description: Clears one byte and writes the values 15 and 255 to two globals, then returns. The facts record that the audio and DMA control registers ADKCON and DMACON are touched by callers of this routine, but the shown code only writes globals.
